newsitem.title: USA: National Processing sees some H2 improvement.
newsitem.headline: National Processing sees some H2 improvement.

text.p: National Processing Inc said Monday its second-quarter net income declined primarily due to narrower margins in the Merchant Services division and higher overhead expenses, offset by increased interest income and lower income taxes, but the company anticipates "some improvement" in the second half.

"While 1997 results to date continue to lag the prior year, we were pleased with the increase relative to the first quarter and expect further progress in the second half," said chief executive Robert Showalter. "Margins appear to have stabilized and we anticipate some improvements in the second half through realization of operating efficiencies and a more favorable business mix."
Earnings per share were further affected by the company's initital public offering of 7.5 million shares in August 1996, which increased the shares outstanding to 50.6 million from 43.1 million.
The company reported net income for the the three months ended June 30 fell to $0.14 per share, or $7.1 million from $0.17 per share or $7.4 million in the same period a year earlier.
